newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Russians seize 150 kg Afghan opium on Tajik border.
newsitem.headline: Russians seize 150 kg Afghan opium on Tajik border.

text.p: Russian border guards have seized 150 kg (330 lbs) of raw opium, one of the biggest hauls of drugs from nearby Afghanistan since the start of the year, the Russian military said on Monday.
"This was one of the largest amount of drugs which traders from Afghanistan tried to smuggle into Tajikistan," a spokesman for Russian border guards told Reuters in the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

He said three armed men tried to cross the border Pyandzh river in two dinghies late on Sunday. Russian border guards opened fire at the trespassers, and minutes later the stream brought the boats to the Tajik side.
"It was not immediately clear if the trespassers were killed, but the guards found 150 kg of raw opium in the dinghies," the official said.
He said that since the start of the year Russian border guards had intercepted around 800 kg (1,780 lbs) of drugs -- mostly raw opium -- from Afghanistan.

Russia keeps some 20,000 its soldiers in Tajikistan, guarding the central Asian state's mountainous border with Afghanistan. They view themselves as a shield against a possible advent of militant Islam.
Last Friday Tajikistan's secular government and the Islamic opposition signed a final peace agreement in Moscow which ended a four-year civil war.
But the fragile peace is often disturbed by maverick bands and drug traders operating out of bases on Afghan territory.
